title: Introduce RAG Playbook Composer docs with live snippets and local eval playground
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an interactive 'Playbook Composer' docs page with editable RAG templates, live snippets, and a devcontainer-backed local eval playground. Includes structured-output tests and telemetry probes. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: Teams frequently need a concise way to prototype retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) playbooks that combine multiple tools, structured-output contracts, and stepwise agent logic. Current docs provide many examples, but onboarding remains scattered: users copy snippets across pages, hand-roll devcontainers, and lack a safe local eval loop for iterating templates. This PR introduces a composable Playbook Composer in the docs site and a small local eval playground to accelerate experimentation and reduce friction.

What this PR adds (single continuous description): Added a new docs page 'RAG Playbook Composer' that surfaces a set of curated, editable playbook templates (single-tool, tool-chaining, multi-step assistants, and stepwise deterministic flows). Each template is backed by a live snippet editor embedded in the docs (CodeMirror) with a sandbox runner button that posts the template to the local eval playground service. The local eval playground runs in a devcontainer and provides deterministic, configurable stubs for retrieval, tool mocks, and tokenized logs so users can iterate without hitting production services. The composer also includes structured-output linting hooks and a small set of assertion templates to validate JSON/CSV outputs.

Files added/changed (high level): docs/rag/playbook-composer.md (new page and guide), docs/snippets/playbooks/* (four new JSON playbook templates), examples/rag-local-eval/ (a tiny Node-based playground with devcontainer and docker-compose shim), static/js/playbook-composer.js (client glue for live snippets and run button), tests/docs/playbook-contracts.test.js (structured output assertions used by CI). Small updates to mkdocs config and sitemap for navigation.

How to run locally: 1) Clone repo and open docs in VS Code, 2) Open the provided devcontainer (./examples/rag-local-eval/.devcontainer) or run docker-compose up -d in examples/rag-local-eval, 3) Start mkdocs serve --dirtyreload in repo root (docs page will connect to local eval at http://localhost:8085 by default). The local eval exposes configuration for retrieval stubs (fixture sets), tool adapter mocks, and an assert endpoint that runs the structured-output tests.

Checklist: - [x] Add new docs page and navigation entry - [x] Add 4 curated templates and live snippet editor - [x] Add small local eval playground + devcontainer - [x] Add unit tests for structured-output assertions - [x] Add telemetry probe hooks to track snippet runs (opt-out) - [x] CI smoke tests (mkdocs build + run playground smoke) pass

Compatibility and scope: This PR is docs and examples only; it introduces a small optional example service intended for local use. No changes to the Redwood API, runtime, or SDKs. Playbook JSON schema is compatible with existing authoring tooling; minor helper keys added are documented on the composer page.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on docs clarity, usability of the composer UX, and the safety of the playground stubs. The playground intentionally returns deterministic fixtures but logs redacted inputs; telemetry events are coarse-grained and opt-out via a local config. See commit messages for incremental changes.

Related work: Builds on ENG-2145 (playbook authoring infrastructure) and PM-483 (improve onboarding for RAG templates).

Merge rationale: Low risk, high developer productivity gains; example code gated in examples/ and opt-in by default.

feat: embed live snippet editor and run button with playbook-composer.js

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice UX idea. Can we make the devcontainer optional and add a short section on resource requirements? Also please ensure the local eval does not attempt outbound network calls by default.

Maya Chen (author): Good call — added a 'Local resource & network' subsection in the docs and disabled outbound calls in the default docker-compose profile. Updated examples/rag-local-eval/docker-compose.yml to use an internal-only network.
Lena Gómez: Docs look solid. Two small copy edits and please add an example that shows a failed assertion case so users can see expected output diffs in logs.
Maya Chen (author): Added failing-case example template (docs/snippets/playbooks/structured-output-template.json) and test that shows assertion diff in CI logs. Updated test to emit readable diffs.
Samir Desai: Can we add telemetry opt-out instructions and a short privacy note?

Maya Chen (author): Added 'Telemetry & privacy' paragraph to playbook-composer.md. Local telemetry is opt-out via examples/rag-local-eval/config.json and by default is disabled in the devcontainer profile.
Lena Gómez: Approved after requested edits.

Add RAG Playbook Composer docs, live snippets, and local eval playground

- 4 curated playbook templates and live snippet editor
- Local eval playground with devcontainer and tests
- CI smoke tests and structured-output assertions
